sources.title: Anders Bjorner and Francesco Brenti, Combinatorics of Coxeter Groups (Graduate Texts in Mathematics 231, Springer 2005; author-hosted complete PDF)
sources.locator: Chapter 1 Section 1.4 (equation (1.20), Corollary 1.4.6, Proposition 1.4.7 and Corollary 1.4.8), printed pp. 17-18; Chapter 2 Section 2.3 (Propositions 2.3.1 and 2.3.2, Corollary 2.3.3), printed pp. 36-37; Chapter 3 Sections 3.1-3.2 in full through Theorem 3.2.7, printed pp. 65-74; read from the extracted full text at harvest time. Sections 3.3-3.4 and the remainder of the book were not read for this batch.

contents.name: Definition 3.1.1: right weak order u<=_R w iff w = u s_1...s_k with every partial product length-additive, and the mirrored left weak order
Proposition 3.1.2(i): one-to-one correspondence between reduced decompositions of w and maximal chains in [e,w]_R
Proposition 3.1.2(ii): u <=_R w iff l(u) + l(u^{-1}w) = l(w)
Proposition 3.1.2(iii): if W is finite then w <=_R w_0 for all w
Proposition 3.1.2(iv): the prefix property (reduced expression of u extends to one of w)
Proposition 3.1.2(v): the chain property of weak order (all maximal chains in an interval have the same length)
Proposition 3.1.2(vi): if s is a left descent of u and of w then u <=_R w iff su <=_R sw
Proposition 3.1.3 with proof: u <=_R w iff T_L(u) subset T_L(w), the converse by the explicit prefix-reflection induction
Corollary 3.1.4: w -> T_L(w) is an order-preserving and rank-preserving embedding into the lattice of finite subsets of T
Proposition 3.1.5: for finite W the maps w -> w_0 w and w -> w w_0 are antiautomorphisms and w -> w_0ww_0 is an automorphism
contents.reason: No item of this pair uses an antiautomorphism of the weak order. The finite-lattice clause of this page uses only the common upper bound w_0; the complement/opposition structure belongs to the finite reflection pages and is not promised by the CG-18 design.

contents.name: Proposition 3.1.6 with proof: for u <=_R w the map x -> ux is an isomorphism [e,u^{-1}w]_R -> [u,w]_R with length additivity
Corollaries 3.1.7 and 3.1.8: rank sizes of weak intervals bounded by binomial coefficients, and finitely many isomorphism types of intervals of each length
contents.reason: The enumeration of interval types is not used by any item of this pair; the page needs only finiteness and gradedness of intervals, which are supplied by the graded lemma.

contents.name: Theorem 3.2.1 with full proof: right weak order is a complete meet-semilattice; every nonempty subset has a meet, and bounded nonempty subsets have joins; finite W is a lattice
Corollary 3.2.2: right order on a finite Coxeter group with x -> xw_0 is an ortholattice
contents.reason: The ortholattice structure is a strengthening not promised by the design and not consumed by any item; it rests on the antiautomorphism of Proposition 3.1.5 and is not needed for the lattice operations proved here.

contents.name: Lemma 3.2.3 with proof: the join of J subset S exists iff W_J is finite, and then equals w_0(J); if W_J is infinite then J has no upper bound
Lemma 3.2.4: if w is a minimal (resp. maximal) coset representative along J with W_J finite then the join of {ws : s in J} is w w_0(J)
contents.reason: Lemma 3.2.4 is used by BB only in the proof of the automorphism theorem 3.2.5; the one- and two-sided covers of a weak interval are not promised by this pair, and the coset formalism is homed on the parabolic coset page (batch 10).

contents.name: Theorem 3.2.5 and Corollary 3.2.6: recovery of the group multiplication from the meet operation, under the disjoint-infinity condition on the Coxeter diagram
contents.reason: The reconstruction theorem and its diagram-automorphism corollary belong to the structure theory of weak order and are not promised by the CG-18 design; no item of this run consumes them.

contents.name: Theorem 3.2.7: the homotopy type of the order complex of an open weak interval and the Mobius function of weak order
contents.reason: No item of this pair uses the order complex or Mobius function of weak intervals; the Mobius/incidence material of this run concerns Bruhat intervals and incidence algebras, and reproducing Theorem 3.2.7 would be a separate proof obligation.

contents.name: Corollary 1.4.6 with the definitions of D_L and D_R: a simple reflection is a left (resp. right) descent iff some reduced expression of w begins (resp. ends) with it
Proposition 1.4.7 (deletion property) and Corollary 1.4.8(i): every non-reduced word can be shortened by deleting two letters, and every expression contains a reduced expression as a subword
Proposition 2.3.1(ii) with proof: if D_L(x) = S then W is finite and x = w_0 (BB prove u <= x in Bruhat order by the lifting property)
Proposition 2.3.2(ii)-(iv), Corollary 2.3.3: the length formulas l(w_0 w) = l(w w_0) = l(w_0) - l(w), w_0^2 = 1 and l(w_0) = |T| for finite W
Sections 3.3-3.4 and Chapters 5-8 (Matsumoto theory, fully commutative elements, heaps, enumerative applications)
contents.reason: These chapters were not read for this batch; the corresponding material is supplied by other pairs of the run (Matsumoto by batch 2, heaps and fully commutative elements by batch 28), so no result from them is claimed or consumed here.

sources.title: John R. Stembridge, On the fully commutative elements of Coxeter groups (J. Algebraic Combin. 1 (1992) 105-134; author-hosted preprint)
sources.locator: Section 1.3 'The weak order', PDF pp. 5-6, and the adjacent paragraph of Section 1.3 recording Proposition 1.4, Proposition 1.5 and the D_R/D_L coset conventions (PDF pp. 6-7); read from the extracted full text. Sections 2-9 (heaps, fully commutative elements, minuscule quotients) were not read.

contents.name: Section 1.3: the right weak order as the transitive closure of the relations w <_R ws for l(w) < l(ws), equivalently x <=_R xy iff xy is reduced; left order and the inversion isomorphism w -> w^{-1}
Proposition 1.3 with proof: if x <=_R y then {w : x <=_R w <=_R y} is isomorphic to {w : w <=_R x^{-1}y} via w -> x^{-1}w
Remark after Proposition 1.3: by a theorem of Bjorner every subinterval of the weak order is at least a lattice
The paragraph introducing D_R(w) and D_L(w) and the coset sets W^J and ^JW with their coset-representative characterizations
Proposition 1.4: the fully commutative elements form an order ideal of the right (and left) weak order
contents.reason: Fully commutative elements and their weak-order ideals are the subject of the heaps page of this run (batch 28); this pair promises only the weak order, its inversions and its lattice operations.

contents.name: Proposition 1.5 with proof: ^JW (resp. W^J) is an order ideal of the right (resp. left) weak order
contents.reason: The ideal property of one-sided parabolic quotient sets is not used by any item of this pair; the quotient sets are defined and applied on the parabolic coset page (batch 10), to which the reader is referred.

contents.name: Sections 2-9: heaps and reduced words, fully commutative classification, minuscule and d-complete quotients, Bruhat order comparisons
contents.reason: Not read for this batch and not consumed here; the corresponding reach results live on the heaps page (batch 28) and on the Bruhat page (batch 12).

sources.title: Nathan Reading and David E. Speyer, Cambrian fans (J. Eur. Math. Soc. 11 (2009) 407-447; arXiv:math/0606201v2)
sources.locator: Section 2 'The weak order', arXiv pp. 5-7 (through the discussion of join-irreducibles and cover reflections); read from the extracted full text. Sections 3-8 (Cambrian congruences, fans, cluster complexes) were not read.

contents.name: Section 2: inversion sets I(w) = {t in T : l(tw) < l(w)}, the uniqueness of w for a given I(w), and the (right) weak order as the partial order induced by containment of inversion sets
Section 2: the weak order is equivalently the transitive closure of the cover relations w < ws for l(w) < l(ws), and equivalently the prefix order on reduced words
Section 2: 'The weak order is known to be a lattice when W is finite', with w_0 as the unique maximal element
Section 2: conjugation by w_0 is an automorphism, w -> ww_0 is an antiautomorphism, and I(ww_0) = T minus I(w)
contents.reason: The opposition antiautomorphism and the complement of the inversion set are not promised by the CG-18 design and no item of this pair consumes them; the finite-lattice clause needs only the common upper bound w_0.

contents.name: Section 2, Proposition 2.1: covered elements of a finite lattice and of a lattice quotient; the congruence-theoretic framework (classes are intervals, monotone endpoint maps)
contents.reason: Lattice congruences and their classes are the subject of the finite-lattice-projection page (batch 5) and of the sortable/Cambrian page (batch 32); this pair needs only the weak order itself and its meet and join operations.

contents.name: Sections 3-8: c-Cambrian congruences, c-sortable elements, Cambrian fans, cluster lattices, and the combinatorial isomorphism
contents.reason: Not read for this batch and not consumed here; the sortable/Cambrian material is scaffolded by batch 32 of this run.
